correctness.rationale: After choosing a basis adapted to the induced projection, lift retained generators by F(u) and discarded generators by w-F(w). The lifts give an automorphism because they are the identity on degree one and hence on the associated graded, and they conjugate F to the standard generator projection in all characteristics. The retained generators freely generate the image; D_c(r) is strictly increasing by the Hall dimensions (the degree-one part already strictly increases). For each r-plane U there are q^{r S_c(d)} choices of lifts of a basis, each generating an eligible image. A given image is counted q^{r S_c(r)} times: all lifts in that image generate it and differ by its higher-degree part. With that choice of free generators, a retraction fixes the first r and maps the other d-r arbitrarily into the image, giving q^{(d-r)D_c(r)} maps per image; this gives the stated polynomial, including zero and identity. With c and q fixed the log of the coefficient equals d^{c+1} f_c(r/d)/c + O(d^c) uniformly. The derivative first increases and then decreases, is positive at 1/2 and negative at 1; the unique maximizer gives a uniform positive gap on every nonempty excluded compact set, while the nearest lattice rank attains the leading exponent. This proves the concentration bound, the rank fraction, and the entropy limit.
residual_risks: The independent enumeration is bounded to the specified F_2 examples; the general statement uses the proof, not their exhaustion. The probability result does not allow c or q to vary with d.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The analogous method does not transplant the census by a change of variables: one must establish conjugation and count lifts for the higher-degree Lie filtration, and then develop the uniform Witt asymptotic.
